critical_caution: This is a curated letters volume, the largest in the Underwood Books series; publisher disclaimers on companion volumes in the same series note the letters cannot be treated as reliable reporting about third parties.

work.title: The Selected Letters of Philip K. Dick: 1972-1973

reading.synopsis: At 423 pages, this is the largest volume in the Underwood Books Selected Letters series, documenting one of the most turbulent and transformative periods in Dick's life: the mysterious 1971 break-in at his San Rafael home, his 1972 trip to Vancouver for a science fiction convention where he delivered the speech 'The Android and the Human,' his brief sojourn in Canada, a suicide attempt, his entry into the X-Kalay drug rehabilitation program, and his eventual relocation to Orange County, California. The volume opens with a comprehensive bibliography of Dick's published novels from Solar Lottery (1955) through Dr. Bloodmoney and beyond.

structure.form: letter collection, chronologically arranged, with prefatory bibliography

motifs: Personal crisis (suicide attempt, drug rehabilitation) documented in real time through correspondence
Geographic relocation as a marker of a major life transition, from Northern California through Canada to Orange County
reading.significance: These letters provide essential primary documentation of the most dramatic biographical rupture in Dick's adult life, immediately preceding the 1974 religious experiences that would reshape his final decade of writing.
reading.closing_note: The volume's span -- from the unresolved 1971 break-in through the crisis and rehabilitation that followed -- captures Dick at his most personally destabilized, just before the theological reorientation of 2-3-74.
